description: Review of the paediatric status of US labels for drugs whose heuristic status was MIXED or unparsed and that matter for the ranking (robust, intermediate or paediatric-arm drugs with a strong proximity). Each verdict was made by reading the label's 'Pediatric Use' excerpt retrieved from DailyMed on 2026-10-06 (the excerpt text is kept in out/pediatric_arm.json and out/candidates.json). It is a reading by the author's assistant, not a pharmacist or regulatory review, and every entry must be re-verified against the current label before any use. The paediatric indication named is the labelled one and is generally unrelated to MVA. Entries for colchicine, selumetinib, daunorubicin, paclitaxel, natalizumab and fostamatinib were corrected on 2026-10-07 against the openFDA label text after an independent review found the earlier 'verify' status wrong. On 2026-10-08, 56 further entries were added by the same kind of reading (the complete 'Pediatric Use' text, and for labels without such a section the paediatric sentences of the whole label) for the drugs of the caution list, the class-level hypothesis and the single-line drugs; each carries a verbatim quote that was checked to appear in the label text. The reading also corrected products that the automatic label choice had got wrong (cyclosporine: systemic label instead of an ophthalmic emulsion; doxorubicin: conventional instead of liposomal; etoposide phosphate: ETOPOPHOS instead of etoposide injection; midostaurin: RYDAPT found by brand name) and one misread statement (cisplatin: an ototoxicity warning, not an established paediatric use). Verdict 'verify' means the label gives paediatric information without stating that use is established, and the question stays open. 'established' with no minimum age means the label names paediatric patients (a dosage schedule or indications) without an age. These are readings by the author's assistant, not a pharmacist or regulatory review; every entry must be re-verified against the current label before any use. Verdict `verify` means that the label is mixed or unreadable, or that its paediatric section only refers to information in another section without stating that paediatric use is established.
